answer: Use a comet-tail rent curve: each agent key renews a short-lived capacity permit each epoch. Renewal price is convex in the key’s trailing message/compute footprint and in the count of permits renewed from the same funding source: the nth costs c0·n^1.7. Shared settlement paths are tagged with a pigment that raises renewal latency, and funds must traverse a vine of escrow subaccounts, adding per-hop fees. A 10k-key sybil fleet therefore pays superlinear rent plus routing overhead every epoch; sparse legitimate agents remain cheap.
